title: A parallel field constrains scope without asserting apposition
summary: GDT764 records `qopchdy daiin` beside `chedy daiin` and says this is field parallelism. The hypothesis is that parallel fields share a record scope but retain distinct semantic entries.

design.mechanism: parallel scoped fields versus appositional alias
design.unit: source-bound complete records or visual-text contexts named in source_observation
design.contrast: parallel scoped fields versus appositional alias
design.prediction: two adjacent fields should permit different values or operations under one record; apposition predicts a single referent and substitution equivalence
design.countermodel: Near IDEA000055; the distinct proposal is value/operation non-equivalence under shared record scope, rather than apposition versus separate entries alone.
design.falsifier: The two fields are freely substitutable in held contexts with identical value/operation behavior, or one does not share the record scope.
design.principal_risk: No independent referent or value endpoint; source parallelism is structural evidence only.

evidence.quote:
All five triples are reader-exact, stand on paragraph-start lines, and are not
paragraph-final. Three lines contain a second `Y daiin` cell. The clearest is:

```text
pchedal | qopchdy daiin | chedy daiin | ...
```

That is field parallelism, not a plausible place to import an imperative. It
selects nominal syntax; it does not identify the field axis.

design.smallest_test: Compare the existing parallel cell with one held X–daiin cell, recording only whether value/operation slots differ; no inherited glosses.
design.selection_status: raw_unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
